result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You fell at home and hit your head on 14 October 2026. You went to the Emergency Department.

Tests showed:
- You did not lose consciousness (pass out)
- There is no fracture (broken bone) in your right hip
- There is no bleeding inside your head

The doctors found that your blood pressure drops when you stand up. When lying down, it was 142/80. When standing up, it dropped to 108/66.

Your medicine (amlodipine) may be causing this drop in blood pressure when you stand.

## What you need to do

1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 milligrams. It may make your blood pressure drop when you stand up.
2. Stand up slowly.
3. Sit on the edge of the bed for 1 minute before standing.
4. Your GP will check your lying and standing blood pressure in 4 weeks.
5. The Falls Prevention Clinic will write to you with an appointment.

## Dates and medicines

**Seen in Emergency Department:** 14 October 2026

**Medicine to stop:**
Amlodipine 10 milligrams — Stop taking this. It may make your blood pressure drop when you stand.

**Your GP will do:**
Check your lying and standing blood pressure in 4 weeks.

**Falls Prevention Clinic:**
They will write to you with an appointment date.

## Questions to ask your doctor

1. Can I take a different blood pressure medicine instead of amlodipine?
2. How long should I wait before doing my normal activities?
3. What can I do to prevent another fall?

## When to get urgent help

If you develop a worsening headache, vomiting (being sick), confusion or drowsiness in the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
